title: PTM-Related Signatures Predict Lymph Node Metastasis and Shape Microenvironment in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Single-Cell and Bulk Integrated Analysis.
authors: Ai, Zhu; Liang, Yuying; Cai, Yuzhi; Gao, Jian; Ren, Lin; Wang, Qiong; Chen, Yutong; Huang, Yongye; Xiang, Zhiming
one_liner_zh: 该研究基于单细胞和bulk转录组数据构建肝细胞癌淋巴结转移的PTM相关预后模型，虽涉及转录因子活性分析，但核心是临床预后与肿瘤微环境，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has a poor prognosis with lymph node metastasis (LNM), severely impacting survival. Protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate tumor microenvironment (TME) dynamics, but their role in HCC LNM is unknown. METHODS: This study systematically analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and bulk transcriptomic data from TCGA-LIHC and validation cohorts. Key cellular subpopulations and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified. PTM-related candidate genes were identified through intersection analysis. Prognostic genes were determined via Cox regression and integrated into a random survival forest (RSF) model. Patients were stratified to assess associations with TME remodeling, genomic alterations, immune checkpoints, and drug sensitivity. Pseudotime trajectory and transcription factor activity analyses elucidated molecular dynamics. RESULTS: Hepatocyte populations were significantly expanded in both LNM and non-LNM HCC groups. The intersection of scRNA-seq DEGs, bulk DEGs, and PTM-related genes identified five candidate genes, among which PJA1 and RFPL4B identified as potential prognostic risk factors and were incorporated into a robust RSF model. High-risk patients exhibited poor survival outcomes, increased tumor mutational burden, and pronounced tumor microenvironment alterations. PJA1 expression was negatively correlated with hepatocyte infiltration. Pseudotime analysis revealed that LNM-associated hepatocytes were arrested in early differentiation states, coinciding with dysregulated transcription factor activity. CONCLUSION: This study computationally identified PJA1 and RFPL4B as post-translational modification-related candidate prognostic genes potentially associated with HCC LNM. The proposed risk model stratified patients into subgroups characterized by distinct tumor microenvironment features and genomic instability. Computational analysis suggested that arrest of hepatocyte differentiation and dysregulation of transcription factor networks may be implicated in metastatic progression, thereby offering novel therapeutic insights.
abstract_zh: 背景：肝细胞癌（HCC）伴淋巴结转移（LNM）预后不良，严重影响生存。蛋白质翻译后修饰（PTMs）调控肿瘤微环境（TME）动态，但其在HCC LNM中的作用尚不清楚。方法：本研究系统分析了来自TCGA-LIHC和验证队列的单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）和批量转录组数据。鉴定了关键细胞亚群和差异表达基因（DEGs）。通过交集分析识别PTM相关候选基因。利用Cox回归确定预后基因，并将其整合到随机生存森林（RSF）模型中。对患者进行分层，以评估与TME重塑、基因组改变、免疫检查点和药物敏感性的关联。拟时序轨迹和转录因子活性分析阐明了分子动态。结果：在LNM和非LNM HCC组中，肝细胞群体均显著扩增。scRNA-seq DEGs、批量DEGs和PTM相关基因的交集识别出五个候选基因，其中PJA1和RFPL4B被确定为潜在预后风险因素，并纳入稳健的RSF模型。高风险患者表现出较差的生存结局、增加的肿瘤突变负荷和显著的肿瘤微环境改变。PJA1表达与肝细胞浸润呈负相关。拟时序分析显示，LNM相关肝细胞停滞在早期分化状态，与转录因子活性失调相一致。结论：本研究通过计算分析将PJA1和RFPL4B鉴定为可能与HCC LNM相关的翻译后修饰相关候选预后基因。所提出的风险模型将患者分为具有不同肿瘤微环境特征和基因组不稳定性的亚组。计算分析提示，肝细胞分化停滞和转录因子网络失调可能参与转移进展，从而提供新的治疗见解。
